career_ladder.note: Judicial officers in Jharkhand are appointed as Civil Judge (Junior Division) / Judicial Magistrate First Class (JMFC) under the Jharkhand Judicial Service (Recruitment and Conditions of Service) Rules. Remuneration and promotion stages follow the Second National Judicial Pay Commission (SNJPC) uniform pay matrix as mandated by the Supreme Court of India in All India Judges Association v. Union of India. Officers advance through Assured Career Progression (ACP) increments at 5-year intervals and promotional cadres up to the High Court of Jharkhand.

exam_scheme.note: The Jharkhand Judicial Service (Civil Judge Junior Division) Examination is conducted in three successive stages: Preliminary Entrance Test (Objective Type screening of 100 marks), Main Examination (Conventional descriptive written test across 4 papers of 100 marks each, 400 marks total), and Viva-Voce Test (100 marks). Final merit list is prepared on the combined aggregate of Main Examination and Viva-Voce (out of 500 marks).

stages.source_label: JPSC Civil Judge (Junior Division) Advt. No. 22/2023 Notification & Syllabus

papers.paper_name: Preliminary Entrance Test (Objective Type General English, GK & Core Laws)
papers.negative_marking: No negative marking (1 mark per correct answer; 0 mark penalty for incorrect responses)
papers.qualifying_threshold: Screening test to shortlist candidates up to 15 times the total vacancies category-wise for the Main Examination. Marks do not count for final merit.

stages.source_label: JPSC Civil Judge (Junior Division) Advt. No. 22/2023 Notification & Syllabus

papers.paper_name: Paper I: Procedural Law (CPC 1908 & CrPC 1973), Indian Penal Code 1860, Indian Evidence Act 1872 & Limitation Act 1963
papers.qualifying_threshold: Compulsory paper counted in merit list

papers.paper_name: Paper II: Law of Contract 1872, Sale of Goods Act 1930, Negotiable Instruments Act 1881, Arbitration and Conciliation Act 1996 & Transfer of Property Act 1882
papers.qualifying_threshold: Compulsory paper counted in merit list

papers.paper_name: Paper III: Hindu Law and Mohammedan Law, Rent Control Law, Specific Relief Act 1963 & Jurisprudence
papers.qualifying_threshold: Compulsory paper counted in merit list

papers.paper_name: Paper IV: Language (Hindi & English — Essay, Precis Writing, Translation & Paraphrase)
papers.qualifying_threshold: Compulsory paper counted in merit list

stages.source_label: JPSC Civil Judge (Junior Division) Advt. No. 22/2023 Notification & Syllabus

papers.qualifying_threshold: Minimum qualifying marks: 25% (25 marks out of 100) for General / EWS candidates; 20% (20 marks out of 100) for SC/ST/EBC & BC candidates. Failure to secure the minimum threshold disqualifies the candidate irrespective of Main written marks.

financial_package.note: Judicial officers in Jharkhand receive remuneration governed by the Second National Judicial Pay Commission (SNJPC) uniform pay matrix as mandated by the Supreme Court of India in All India Judges Association v. Union of India. While JPSC Advertisement No. 22/2023 specifies the unrevised pay scale of ₹27,700–44,770, judicial appointments in Jharkhand are placed in the revised SNJPC Pay Scale Level J-1 (₹77,840–₹1,36,520).
financial_package.pay_source_label: JPSC Civil Judge (Junior Division) Advt. No. 22/2023 & SNJPC Recommendations in WP(C) 643/2015
financial_package.estimate_note: Gross salary computed from Level J-1 entry basic ₹77,840 + 58% DA (₹45,147) + judicial HRA (8%–16% or official government judicial bungalow) + judicial sumptuary, robe, medical, conveyance, and domestic help allowances. In-hand estimate reflects standard statutory deductions including 10% NPS (Basic + DA), GIS, and Professional Tax.
official_perks: Official designated judicial residence / government bungalow in posting district
Sumptuary allowance and robe allowance per SNJPC recommendations
Conveyance allowance / official vehicle with driver and fuel entitlement
Medical facilities and reimbursement for officer and dependent family members
Electricity and water charge reimbursement up to prescribed monthly units
Residential orderly / attendant allowance and telephone/broadband reimbursement
